edits.text: Keep a finite verb or auxiliary together with the immediately following core complement (direct object, essential prepositional object, or clausal/complement phrase) when that complement begins within the next 1–4 source tokens.

Keep a numeral or quantifier token (digits or spelled-out) together with the immediately following unit or measurement phrase (unit words, currency symbol, % or parenthetical unit) when that unit begins within four tokens.

- As a last resort, order candidate cuts on the source surface as follows: prefer a cut at a punctuation or clause boundary (comma, semicolon, sentence break) over a cut that separates a finite verb or auxiliary from its immediately following core complement (direct object, essential prepositional object, or clausal complement); prefer those over cuts that split a numeral or quantifier token (digits or spelled-out) from its immediately following unit or measurement phrase (units, currencies, percentages, or parenthetical units).

- As a last resort, order candidate cuts on the source surface as follows: prefer a cut that leaves a numeral or quantifier token (digits or spelled-out) attached to its immediately following unit or measurement phrase over one that does not; if tied, prefer a cut that keeps a finite verb or auxiliary adjacent to its immediately following core complement (direct object, essential prepositional object, or clausal complement) over one that does not; otherwise prefer a cut at a punctuation or clause boundary (comma, semicolon, sentence break).

Keep a finite verb or auxiliary together with the immediately following core complement (direct object, essential prepositional object, or clausal/complement phrase) when that complement begins within the next four tokens.

- Prefer a cut immediately before a finite verb or auxiliary token over a cut that falls between that verb and its immediately following core complement (direct object, essential prepositional object, or clausal complement) when that complement begins within the next 1–4 tokens.
